Models from the United States and around the world provide a roadmap for how electric rail infrastructure is built, owned, and operated. Railroads, public agencies, and electric utilities could be owners of rail electrification infrastructure. Identifying viable financing models is key to the success of rail electrification. Infrastructure permitting. Charging infrastructure for zero-emission technology must be designed, permitted, and constructed. Wait times vary greatly by utility and region, with some utilities able to provide rail yard charging infrastructure in a matter of a few months, and other utilities facing multi-year-long delays. Developing a streamlined permitting process for charging infrastructure could reduce wait times to deploy zero-emission technologies. Assured, reliable railroad funding.
